newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas called higher on firmer cash.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas called higher on firmer cash.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures were expected to open higher Thursday as early talk of firmer cash prices enticed some buyers to the market, industry sources said.
May over-the-counter trade ranged from $2.01 to $2.03 after settling Wednesday at $2.005 per million British thermal units.
In ACCESS, May last traded near the session high at $2.019, up 1.4 cents from the regular session.
Cash prices at the Henry Hub, La., were talked about three to five cents higher at $2.05-2.07 per mmBtu.
Triggering the uptick in cash, traders said, was the colder weather moving into the Northeast, which was expected to bring heavy precipitation possibly in the form of snow in the higher elevations.
Temperatures throughout the East and upper Midwest are expected to remain below normal through the weekend before turning milder early next week.
Traders said resistance in May was at $2.02 and then at $2.05, $2.07 and $2.095. Support points were seen at $1.925, $1.88, $1.85 and $1.825.
"The May/June spread didn't narrow. If this was a bullish market, it should have narrowed," one market source said.
The May/June spread as of April 16 was at 4.1 cents.

In Wednesday's cash market, Gulf Coast prices were steady to up slightly in the high-$1.90s to about $2. Midcontinent pipes were little changed in the mid-$1.80s. Gas at the New York city gate was quoted up slightly to the mid-to-high $2.30s.

AGA said Wednesday that U.S. gas stocks fell last week by 16 bcf. Overall stocks are still 290 bcf, or 53 percent, above year-ago. Eastern inventories, which fell last week by 23 bcf, are still more than double 1996's record lows.
